name: shop
prompt: The inside of a small radio repair shop, its back wall seen straight on, as in the layout. From left to right: an old wooden back door standing ajar; a fuse box and a calendar on the wall above a patch of bare brick; a battered leather sofa with a checked blanket and cushions on a worn rug, a floor lamp beside it; a tall wooden shelf unit crowded with old radios, books and boxes; a pegboard of hand tools; a long, high workbench with an old monitor with a green screen, an oscilloscope and a valve amplifier on it, a shelf of old radios above it and drawers below; pinned schematics, a notice, a wall clock and a framed photograph; a corkboard with a map and notes; a desk lamp on an arm. Brick showing through cracked plaster, a tiled wainscot, worn floorboards. Every radio and device is an old relic patched together over decades: steampunk-like contraptions of riveted grey metal, exposed valves, gauges and tangled cables, dented, rusted and taped. Dust, grime and peeling paint everywhere.
concierge: The Concierge's version of the same shop keeps it retro, like a lovingly kept antique radio shop: the radios restored relics in polished walnut, cream bakelite and brass with warm glowing dials; the shelves, the bench and the door polished dark wood; the sofa supple leather with a soft wool blanket; the monitor and the instruments handsome vintage pieces with soft green screens; warm brick, clean plaster, tidy tools; warm amber lamplight, clean and cosy, glamorous in a nostalgic way. Same layout.
